Higher exhaled carbon monoxide (CO) levels were associated with a lower risk of Parkinson’s disease in a 12-year study of 512,701 adults in China.

The link was also seen among non-smokers, who had about a one-third lower likelihood of diagnosis at higher CO levels. Among 1,131 cases, smokers showed an approximately 30% lower relative risk.

Led by Oxford researchers, the observational study found no similar association with other neurodegenerative diseases. It does not prove that CO prevents Parkinson’s, and smoking is not a preventive measure: tobacco causes cancer, heart disease and strokes.

Now, Harvard has begun testing a low-dose CO drug in people with Parkinson’s.

🎙 Spokesperson urges international bodies to pursue Iran’s rights over wartime aggression

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian government spokesperson, Fatemeh Mohajerani, has called on international organizations to take an active role in securing the rights of Iranians, saying attacks on the country during two wars imposed by the US and the Israeli regime amounted to acts of terrorism rather than conventional military operations.

Speaking at a Saturday gathering on protecting the right to education through family and school cooperation, Mohajerani said Iran had come under attack twice while negotiations were in progress.
​
She recalled that on the morning of June 13, as enemy aircraft were taking off, the US president posted that he had instructed his administration to pursue negotiations with Iran with full force. Iran had not sought war, she said, adding that it had been imposed on the country and that Iran had defended itself.
​
Mohajerani also recounted her visit to Minab City, following the attack on Shajareh Tayyebeh School. She described the grief of families who lost loved ones, including a teacher whose husband was left to care for their one-and-a-half-year-old twins.
​
She said teachers, school staff and families had worked to keep education going despite the damage. While formal education suffered during the wars, she said, lessons in humanity, solidarity and resilience continued.
​
Mohajerani cited the death of an 11-year-old girl in Yazd, central Iran, from cardiac arrest during an attack, saying Iran would seek redress for every life lost and injury inflicted.
​
She added that online education could not fully replace in-person learning, particularly in skill-based secondary education.

📄 New surprises to be unveiled on battlefield if attacks on Iran resume: IRGC

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Spokesperson for the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi says Iran will unveil new weapons that will astonish the world if a new round of military confrontation erupts with the United States and Israel.

“There are surprises that will be unveiled and deployed on the battlefield if a third wave of confrontation with the enemy erupts. These surprises will astonish the entire world,” Mohebbi said on Saturday at a press conference on the achievements of the IRGC Aerospace Force, held on the occasion of National Aerospace Week.
​
He also said that Iran’s response to any possible new military attacks would be harder than before and leave the enemies crippled for years to come.
​
“If they once again miscalculate, or if the Zionists, in pursuit of their own interests, lead the criminal United States into another miscalculation, they should know that Iran’s next blows will be even harder and will leave them crippled for years to come,” he noted.
​
The spokesperson said that new missile cities would be unveiled as part of the IRGC Aerospace Force’s achievements, adding that these missile production facilities had been moved underground, preventing the enemy from halting missile production even in wartime.
​
Mohebbi said that the IRGC Aerospace Force had strived to produce all its weapons using indigenous know-how and expertise, without importing arms from other countries, inviting foreign military advisors to provide guidance, or resorting to reverse engineering of weapons captured from the enemy.
​
This self-sufficiency in producing weapons, particularly in the aerospace sector, is a “very big achievement,” he stressed.
​
The IRGC Aerospace Force has even managed to export some of its products to other countries, including Arman missiles, 385 drones, and the Third Khordad air defense system, transforming Iran from an importer into an exporter of military equipment, the spokesperson noted.
​
Highlighting other achievements of the IRGC Aerospace Force, Mohebbi said the force had developed operational management capabilities for using light and heavy weapons, as well as long- and short-range systems, during hostile attacks, enabling it to continue its counteroperations without interruption.
​
According to the spokesperson, the IRGC Aerospace Force had helped establish a balance of power and strengthen Iran’s deterrence by developing its missile, drone, and electronic warfare industries. He added that the force had continued producing missiles and drones even during the war in recent months.
